PAGE 11 Original lecture content: TERMS IN LEXICAL ANALYSIS Token: A pair consisting of token name and an optional attribute value. Remember the form <token-name, attribute-value> Pattern: An informal description of a form that lexemes of a token may take. For e.g. if token is a keyword , then pattern is just the sequence of characters that form the keyword. Lexeme: It is an actual stream of characters (in the source program) that matches the pattern and is identified by the lexical analyzer as an instance of that token. PAGE 19 Original lecture content: ▪Most of the times, the lexical analyzer is not able to detect source-code errors. ▪It usually needs aid of other components to perform error-detection. ▪For example: if the source-code (in C language) HANDLING LEXICAL ERRORS encounters 'fi', the lexical analyzer will not detect it as an error and can't tell whether it is a misspelled keyword or an undeclared literal. ▪Since fi is a valid lexeme for the token id, the lexical analyzer must return the token id to the parser and let some other phases (probably the parser in this case) handle an error due to the transposition of letters. CPT316 PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE IMPLEMENTATION AND PARADIGMS

HANDLING LEXICAL ERRORS When none of the patterns for tokens matches a prefix of remaining input. Panic Mode of Error Recovery ▪ The errors due to which lexical analyzer is unable to proceed with compilation, it resorts to panic mode of error recovery. ▪ Delete the successive characters from the remaining input until analyzer can find a well-formed token. CPT316 PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE IMPLEMENTATION AND PARADIGMS

Original lecture content: SINGLE VS TWO-BUFFER Single Buffering Double Buffering/ Two- Buffer ▪The compiler loads a substantial segment of ▪The lexical analyzer processes characters the source file into a buffer. from one buffer ▪The lexical analyzer processes the buffer ▪The second buffer is simultaneously loaded character by character to detect tokens. with the next set of characters from the source file. ▪Once the buffer is depleted, it is refilled with the next set of characters, and the cycle continues. ▪This concurrent processing and reading ensure a steady stream of characters and minimizes wait times. ▪This approach can be inefficient as it requires processing to halt each time the buffer is replenished. PAGE 27 Original lecture content: ▪Size of each buffer is usually N, where N is the size of a disk block. ▪Using one system read command, we can read N INPUT BUFFERING characters into the buffer, rather than using one system call per character. ▪Eof marks the end of source file and is different from any possible character of the source program. CPT316 PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE IMPLEMENTATION AND PARADIGMS Diagram representation / semantic relationships: Buffer-pair relationship: two adjacent input buffer halves are used alternately for scanning.

Then, after the lexeme is recorded as an attribute value of a token returned to the parser, lexemeBegin is set to the character immediately after the lexeme just found. ▪Once the next lexeme is determined, the forward is set to the character at its right CPT316 PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE IMPLEMENTATION AND PARADIGMS Diagram representation / semantic relationships: Two pointers: lexemeBegin marks the start of the current lexeme; forward scans ahead to locate its end.

Original lecture content: SENTINELS ▪Each time we move forward, we must check that we have not moved off one of the buffers. Because if we do, we must reload the other buffer. ▪Thus for each character read, we make two tests: one for the end of buffer and one to determine what character is read. ▪The buffer end test can be combined with the test for the current character if we extend each buffer to hold a sentinel character at the end. ▪Sentinel is the special character that cannot be a part of the source program and the natural choice is eof. CPT316 PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE IMPLEMENTATION AND PARADIGMS Diagram representation / semantic relationships: Sentinel marks the end of a buffer half; when encountered, check whether to refill or terminate.

PAGE 31 Original lecture content: SENTINELS ▪Note that eof retains its use as a marker for the end of entire input. ▪Any eof that appears other than at the end of buffer means that the input is at an end. CPT316 PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE IMPLEMENTATION AND PARADIGMS Diagram representation / semantic relationships: EOF sentinel can represent an end-of-buffer boundary or true end-of-input depending on buffer position and refill result.
